thesisQuality.basis: Strong organic growth, record RPO and broad infrastructure demand support durable adoption/value capture, but project execution remains replicable and customer concentration is incompletely disclosed.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue +19.8%, operating margin 10.6%, EPS +34.8%, RPO +43.9% and raised guidance collectively support the exceptional/strong boundary; value is held near the lower exceptional edge because project conversion and labor costs remain risks.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Independent current data show roughly $33.3B market cap, 23.49 trailing P/E and 21.73 forward P/E: plausible growth-adjusted upside but not clear bargain asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: Raised 2026 revenue/EPS guidance plus record RPO provide identifiable near/medium-term execution catalysts, though RPO timing is not guaranteed.

governancePower.basis: Current filings and operating delivery support adequate-to-strong execution and disclosure; evidence is insufficient for exceptional stewardship or unusually strong alignment.

alignment2036.basis: Electrical/mechanical execution serves data/network, water, healthcare and institutional infrastructure, creating strong exposure to durable infrastructure needs across multiple end markets.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Broad RPO growth across Network and Communications, Water/Wastewater, Institutional and Healthcare shows multiple demand engines reusing core project-execution capabilities.

bottleneckControl.basis: Skilled trades and complex MEP execution are meaningful constraints with qualification/execution friction, but EMCOR does not control an irreplaceable system bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Demand visibility spans several infrastructure verticals, reducing single-theme dependence; project cycles and customer capital spending remain common downside channels.

substitutionResilience.basis: Complex project qualification, local skilled labor and execution capability create moderate replacement barriers, but alternative contractors remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Scale and diversified operations provide some resilience, while skilled-labor and material availability remain meaningful critical dependencies; current evidence does not justify a strong-band score.

pricingPower.basis: 10.6% operating margin alongside strong organic growth supports some economic capture, but current evidence does not isolate durable price pass-through from favorable project mix and demand.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are RPO conversion/timing, labor and material constraints, project mix/cost execution, and incomplete customer-concentration disclosure; none presently contradict the operating thesis.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability are validated; operating evidence is primary and recent; valuation has a current independent source. Confidence is reduced for undisclosed customer concentration and limited independent corroboration of issuer operating claims.

scoreRecord.thesis: EMCOR is a scaled skilled-trade and complex MEP execution platform exposed to durable data/network, water, healthcare and institutional infrastructure demand, with record RPO and strong organic execution providing visibility while labor/project execution limits bottleneck control.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Record RPO may convert later or at lower margins than expected if skilled-labor scarcity, materials, project mix or customer capital-spending conditions deteriorate.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Conversion of record RPO into revenue/margin and delivery against raised 2026 guidance in the next earnings cycle.

scoreBreakdown.method: Methodology 1.0.0 weighted component candidate score; risk and confidence are retained separately for downstream locked-methodology treatment.
